title: Madras High Court restrains thermal power plant workers from going on strike

ai.summary: The Madras High Court restrained Tamil Nadu electricity workers from striking at state thermal power plants, citing concerns over power disruption and legal compliance with strike notices.

facts.claim: The Madras High Court restrained Central Organisation of Tamil Nadu Electricity Employees from going on a strike at the State government run thermal power plants
facts.quote: The Madras High Court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) restrained Central Organisation of Tamil Nadu Electricity Employees, affiliated to the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU), from going on a strike at the State government run thermal power plants from Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

facts.claim: The court issued an interim injunction based on an urgent public interest litigation petition
facts.quote: Second Division Bench of Justices S.M. Subramaniam and R. Rajesh Vivekananthan issued the interim injunction pursuant to an urgent public interest litigation petition filed by activist Vineeth Kumar

facts.claim: The court noted there was no direct employer-employee relationship between the Tamil Nadu Power Generation Corporation Limited and the workers
facts.quote: the judges also recorded the submission of Additional Advocate General P.V. Balasubramaniam that there was no direct employer-employee relationship between the Tamil Nadu Power Generation Corporation Limited (TNPGCL) and the workers who had been engaged for work through various contractors.

facts.claim: The court emphasized that thermal power plants must keep functioning round-the-clock
facts.quote: the Additional Advocate General said that the thermal power generation plants must keep functioning round-the-clock and that it would become very difficult to restart them if there happened to be a temporary shutdown.

facts.claim: The PIL petitioner claimed workers did not give 15 days notice to TNPGCL as required by law
facts.quote: In his affidavit, the PIL petitioner said the workers intending to strike work had not given a 15 days notice to TNPGCL as required under law.

ai.background_note: The court restrained electricity workers from striking at thermal power plants to prevent disruption, following a public interest litigation over legal compliance and operational continuity.
